tagline: KPI dashboards and board reports built from accounting exports.
verdictSummary: A KPI dashboard built from monthly accounting CSV exports — revenue, margin, custom ratios, trend charts, a one-command PDF report — is a real weekend build with zero API keys, since your financials never have to touch a server. What doesn't come with it is live accounting sync, multi-entity consolidation, and forecasting.
coreLoopDIY: Import monthly accounting CSV exports, compute KPIs and custom ratios locally, and generate a dashboard plus a one-command PDF board report.
whyPeopleStillPay: Board and advisor reporting needs to be accurate, comparable month to month, and presentable without extra formatting work — people pay for that reliability and polish, not for the ability to chart a number.
notes: An interesting finance-ops case: charting the numbers is easy, getting the accounting semantics right is the actual work.
prompt:
Build a small-business KPI dashboard that runs entirely on your own machine, with your financials never touching a server: drop monthly accounting CSV exports (profit and loss, balance sheet) into a folder, and parse them into monthly line items in a local database. Compute standard KPIs per month — revenue, gross margin, net profit, cash on hand — plus custom ratios you define as formulas over account names in a config file. Build a dashboard of KPI tiles showing month-over-month change, a 12-month trend chart per KPI, and a drill-down table per account. Let each KPI carry an optional target, shown as a clear over/under indicator. Add a one-command export that renders the dashboard to a PDF board report.

Do not build live accounting API sync, multi-entity consolidation, or forecasting — CSV in, dashboard and PDF out is the honest, complete scope for a personal version, and requires zero API keys.

faq.q: Can I import my existing Fathom HQ setup?
faq.a: Not directly — Fathom's KPI definitions and report templates don't export. Your underlying accounting data, though, is the same monthly CSV export from Xero or QuickBooks either way, so the source data isn't lost.

faq.q: Will it work on my phone?
faq.a: The dashboard renders on a phone browser for a quick check, but importing CSVs and setting up KPI formulas is realistically a desktop task.

faq.q: What does it cost to run?
faq.a: Nothing beyond the machine you already own — no hosting, no API key, no subscription, since everything stays local.

faq.q: What's the one thing that doesn't survive the rebuild?
faq.a: Multi-entity consolidation. Fathom can roll several related businesses into one comparable view; this build handles one set of books at a time, and combining several means doing that math yourself.
